text: It's two a.m. An AI agent with a retry bug is paying for the same API. Again. And again.
Agents pay for data on their own now, over x402.
Most pay from a hot key with no limits. An alert only tells you after the money has moved.
This is Warden. A watchdog for the wallets your agents spend from, on Sui.
Your agents don't pay from their own wallets. They spend through SpendVault, a Move contract Warden can pause on-chain.
You set the rules once, in plain English. Block anything over a dollar a day, and it becomes an on-chain cap.
When something is new, Warden asks you, and explains why in plain words.
Tap Always allow, and your answer becomes a rule. It won't ask about that again.
Back to two a.m. Thirty payments to the same API in ten minutes. Warden pauses the agent on-chain. No confirm button. No human.
The agent keeps trying. The vault refuses, sixty-nine times, and moves nothing. That's a real transaction on Sui, signed by Warden's own key.
Warden watches the vault through Tatum's Sui gateway. One query covers every agent.
And it remembers in Walrus Memory: every rule, incident and reply. On a fresh server, Warden restored itself from Walrus and carried on.
In week one, it asks about everything. As your replies become rules, it asks less.
Your agents can spend. Warden watches.
